conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for capital preservation with lower volatility. Target returns are modest, focusing on stability over aggressive growth. Drawdowns should be minimal, but upside potential is also capped.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs to minimal positions.
Reduce concentration in software ETFs.
Add a new, quality tech name to the portfolio.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth.
It aims for moderate returns with controlled risk.
A small cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced plan seeks risk-first growth by trimming leverage and adding a quality name. It aims for moderate monthly returns while keeping drawdowns in check. Expect a blend of broad market exposure and select tech.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged software ETFs.
Increase exposure to leveraged semiconductor ETFs.
Add a new, quality tech name to the portfolio.

Expect higher potential returns and higher drawdowns.
A small cash buffer will be maintained.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for stretched growth by increasing leverage and concentration in high-potential areas. Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns, especially with leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta software names.
Increase allocation to income-focused ETF.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable distributions.

income.read: This income-focused plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth. It aims for low drawdowns by cutting leverage and high-beta names. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
